rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a written or oral lease without good cause, and must be able to prove the grounds in court. A Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment of rent.

coverage_conditions.text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.

Does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.

rules.title: Eviction for failure to pay rent
rules.requirement: If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may file for eviction without prior notice, except that a 14-day notice is required if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.

tenant evicted. The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an

rules.requirement: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent if the tenant used the unpaid rent to keep utility services going after notice that they were in danger of being discontinued, and the landlord was responsible for those utilities and did not pay. rules.title: Eviction for breach of lease covenants or agreements
rules.requirement: If the tenant continues to substantially breach reasonable lease covenants after a written Notice to Cease and the lease reserves a right of re-entry, the landlord may sue for eviction after a Notice to Quit served at least one month before filing. In public housing, breaches of covenants on illegal drug use or other illegal activities allow eviction without a Notice to Cease, with the Notice to Quit served per federal regulations.

If the tenant continues to substantially violate or breach the reasonable covenants or 
agreements contained in the lease, after given written Notice to Cease violating or 
breaching those covenants or agreements and if the landlord has reserved a right of re-entry 
in the lease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on 
the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for this type of eviction.

rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted when the landlord must board up or demolish due to cited violations, cannot abate violations with the tenant in place, must correct an illegal occupancy, or a government agency is permanently removing the property from the rental market. rules.requirement: A tenant evicted to correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the tenant's monthly rent, paid by the landlord. rules.requirement: A landlord permanently retiring a building or mobile home park from residential use may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.

rules.title: Prohibition on sale of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Selling, licensing or otherwise providing to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley is unlawful. A coordinated pricing algorithm is a process that uses nonpublic Competitor Data less than 90 days old to calculate and recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor.
rules.coverage_conditions: Anyone who sells, licenses or provides coordinated pricing algorithms to City of Berkeley landlords for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Excluded from the definition: products that publish aggregated and anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines; products or processes used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, as long as Competitor Data is not used as an input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.penalty: The City Attorney may file a civil action for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; the court shall award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to the City Attorney if it prevails.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not end a tenancy without just cause. Just cause is either an at-fault cause, such as nonpayment of rent, a material lease breach, nuisance or criminal activity, or a no-fault cause taken in good faith: owner or family move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, a government or court order to vacate, or demolition or substantial remodel.

Tenancies do not include fixed-term leases of three months or less.
